issues.description: Constructor of class Lecture: the problem statement/UML require a constructor that initializes five attributes in this exact order: (lectureName: String, numberOfInscribedStudents: int, numberOfGuestStudents: int, numberOfLecturers: int, numberOfTutors: int). The template implementation currently declares a constructor with only three parameters: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents). The solution repository contains the intended five-parameter constructor. This mismatch leaves students uncertain which constructor signature to implement and will cause confusion or test failures when code or tests expect the five-argument constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Lecture.java to provide the constructor signature that matches the UML and problem statement: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) { ... } and either provide a minimal implementation that assigns parameters to the corresponding fields or remove the incomplete three-argument constructor so students implement the full five-argument constructor themselves. Ensure the parameter order matches the UML (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors).
